findings.summary: Lock-contention path skips the synthesizer yet still runs anchor-check and export. When tryLockSynthesizer() returns null, runGenerate falls through to spawnAnchorCheck and spawnExport, so a full generation pass exports a report for which no synthesizer ever ran — and, in exactly the racing scenario the spec's lock exists for (spec §3: turn interval 600s vs synthesizer 360s), the second turn exports doc(report) while the first turn's synthesizer is still writing it. Spec §3 requires the strict serial edge debater×3 → synthesizer → anchor-check → 导出 and describes the lock as a structural guarantee against two processes operating on the same draft; a named loop-engine lock serializes (wait-then-run), it does not drop the stage. The implemented try-lock-or-skip semantics moves the race from write/write to write/export rather than eliminating it, and the D6 test only asserts the second spawn count, so this fall-through is unobserved.

Spec §6 requires the three debater routes to come from configuration AND be mutually distinct, but GenerateConfig.debaterRoutes is only typed as a 3-tuple of strings with no runtime or type-level distinctness enforcement. Distinctness holds solely because DEFAULT_GENERATE_CONFIG happens to list three different literals, so D5 passes on the default config while any caller-supplied config with duplicate routes is accepted silently — the very failure mode mutation Q2 models.

parseReportMarker matches the marker anywhere in the body rather than at the body head. Spec §5.2 requires the marker to be deterministically parseable from the body header; the unanchored regex will happily return a marker embedded mid-document (for example one quoted inside prose), so the parse is not head-scoped as specified.

Acceptance rows D18 (npm run typecheck / npm test exit 0) and D19 (existing 61 cases not deleted) could not be corroborated from committed evidence at this subject: the only committed acceptance record is from the previous package dev_ledr_s3_terminate_01 (input/subject f0b621b4, 5 files / 61 tests) and predates src/generate.ts. Static counting shows 79 `it(` occurrences across 6 test files (61 pre-existing + 18 new), consistent with the summary's claim, but the pass/exit-0 result rests on IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md alone.
